skill.name: seo-structure-architect
skill.description: Analyzes and optimizes content structure including header hierarchy, suggests schema markup, and internal linking opportunities. Creates search-friendly content organization.
skill.summary: Builds search-friendly content structures with clear headings, internal links, topic clusters, and schema recommendations.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and SEO terminology. The skill provides advisory content-structure guidance and contains no executable commands, network reconnaissance, or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown backticks to format a relative documentation path. It does not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any external command.
Lines 78-84 are a fenced text example showing a heading hierarchy. The backticks delimit Markdown and contain no executable command.
Lines 62-63 list Organization, LocalBusiness, and BreadcrumbList schema types. They do not request network access, host discovery, scanning, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Weak content hierarchy makes pages difficult for readers and search engines to understand. This skill creates structured outlines, linking plans, and schema recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Reviews H1 through H6 hierarchy for logical nesting and topic alignment.
Creates content outlines with primary sections and supporting subsections.
Maps topic clusters, parent pages, child pages, and contextual internal links.
Recommends relevant schema types such as Article, FAQ, HowTo, and BreadcrumbList.
Plans tables of contents, breadcrumbs, jump links, and URL structures.
Suggests list, table, definition, and process formats for featured snippets.
limitations: Does not measure live rankings, traffic, backlinks, or search engine results.
Does not validate schema against a live website or search engine testing tool.
Requires page content, site context, or topic goals for specific recommendations.
Recommendations still require editorial review and environment-specific implementation.

use_cases.title: Restructure a Long Article
use_cases.description: Turn an uneven draft into a logical heading hierarchy with a table of contents and snippet-ready sections.

use_cases.title: Plan a Topic Cluster
use_cases.description: Define pillar and supporting pages, parent-child relationships, and relevant internal links for a subject area.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical SEO Requirements
use_cases.description: Document schema, breadcrumbs, URLs, components, and sitemap priorities for implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Headings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page outline for H1-H6 hierarchy. Identify skipped levels, unclear labels, and duplicated topics. Suggest a corrected outline: [outline]
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused heading review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Content Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an SEO-focused outline for [topic] serving [audience]. Include one H1, logical H2 and H3 sections, and a table of contents.
prompt_templates.scenario: A writer needs a complete structure before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Topic Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a topic cluster for [subject]. Define the pillar page, supporting pages, URL relationships, anchor themes, and contextual internal linking opportunities.
prompt_templates.scenario: An SEO strategist is planning connected content.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Implementation Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this site structure and produce an implementation blueprint: [structure]. Include hierarchy, clusters, internal links, schema priorities, breadcrumbs, snippets, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs advanced editorial and technical requirements.

output_examples.input: Review a guide with an H1 followed by H3 sections and repeated H2 labels.
output: Use one descriptive H1 for the guide topic.
Add distinct H2 sections before each group of H3 subsections.
Replace repeated H2 labels with specific section topics.
Generate the table of contents from the corrected H2 and H3 structure.

output_examples.input: Plan a topic cluster for home solar installation.
output: Pillar page: Complete Guide to Home Solar Installation.
Supporting pages: costs, panel selection, permits, incentives, maintenance, and installer evaluation.
Link supporting pages to the pillar using descriptive contextual anchors.
Cross-link costs with incentives and panel selection when the relationship serves readers.

output_examples.input: Recommend structured data for a step-by-step article with common questions.
output_examples.output: Prioritize Article and BreadcrumbList. Consider HowTo when the visible steps satisfy eligibility requirements, and FAQ when each question and answer appears on the page.

best_practices: Provide the audience, primary topic, existing headings, and page goal before requesting an analysis.
Keep recommendations aligned with visible content and real page relationships.
Validate schema, links, breadcrumbs, and responsive navigation after implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not force keywords into every heading or anchor.
Do not add schema for content that users cannot see on the page.
Do not build isolated topic silos that prevent useful cross-topic navigation.

faq.question: Can this skill rewrite my full article?
faq.answer: It focuses on structure, hierarchy, links, and presentation. It can guide revisions, but full copywriting is outside its primary scope.

faq.question: Does it guarantee higher search rankings?
faq.answer: No. Structure supports clarity and crawlability, but rankings also depend on quality, authority, competition, performance, and other factors.

faq.question: What input produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the page goal, target audience, primary topic, current headings, related pages, platform, and known technical constraints.

faq.question: Can it recommend schema markup?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends suitable schema types, but implementation must match visible content and pass current validation requirements.

faq.question: Can it plan internal links across a website?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the site inventory or relevant URLs so it can map clusters, relationships, anchors, and contextual linking opportunities.

faq.question: Does it access my website or analytics?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow analyzes information supplied in the conversation and does not perform live crawling or analytics retrieval.
